question: In which of the following religions was the agriculture prohibited for its followers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jainism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jainism:**

 
 
• Jainism strongly emphasizes the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence) towards all living beings.
 
• Agriculture is often prohibited for strict Jain followers because it inevitably involves harming living organisms, such as insects and microorganisms in the soil.
 
• Jains believe that even unintentional harm carries karmic consequences.
 
• This is why many Jains traditionally pursue occupations such as trade and commerce.
 
• Jain monks and nuns especially adhere to strict rules to avoid causing any harm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhism:**

 
 
• Buddhism emphasizes the Middle Way, avoiding extremes of asceticism and indulgence.
 
• While Buddhism promotes compassion for all living beings, it does not strictly prohibit agriculture.
 
• Buddhist monks and nuns often rely on alms from lay followers, which may include agricultural produce.
 
• Buddhist teachings focus on achieving enlightenment through meditation and ethical conduct.
 
• Buddhism has varying views on different occupations, but agriculture is not universally prohibited.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• Vaishnavism is a Hindu tradition that centers on the worship of Vishnu or his avatars, such as Krishna and Rama.
 
• Vaishnavism encourages a devotional path to spiritual liberation.
 
• Agriculture is a common occupation among Vaishnavas, and agricultural produce is often offered as prasad (sacred food).
 
• Vaishnavism emphasizes vegetarianism and non-violence, but agriculture is not prohibited.
 
• Many Vaishnavas believe that offering the product of their labor to god is a part of their devotional practice.
 
 
 
• **Shaivism:**
 
 
• Shaivism is a Hindu tradition that centers on the worship of Shiva.
 
• Like Vaishnavism, Shaivism does not prohibit agriculture.
 
• Shaivites engage in various occupations, including agriculture, and often offer agricultural produce in their rituals.
 
• Shaivism emphasizes asceticism and yogic practices, but it does not impose a general prohibition on agriculture.
 
• Shaivism has a diverse range of practices and philosophies.
